newsitem.title: USA: MobileMedia holds payment, debt off lows.
newsitem.headline: MobileMedia holds payment, debt off lows.

text.p: MobileMedia Corp debt rebounded from an eight to nine point spike lower in consolidation after the company's failure to make its $11.7 million November 1 interest payment, traders said.

MobileMedia's 9-3/8 percent debt of 2007 was quoted at 54 bid, 56 offered at mid-morning, about three points below Thursday's close. One trader spotted a brief market of 48 bid, 51 offered in early trade.

David Wells, managing director and analyst at Bear Stearns & Co Inc, said MobileMedia had already telegraphed its intention to the market, noting that the missed payment hardly came as a surprise. He added MobileMedia said it may still make the payment before the 30-day grace period expires.
"The press release really didn't have anything new in it," Wells said, adding, "The numbers were as expected and there were optimistic statements by the CEO as opposed to cautious statements."

Michael Lorelli, president and chief executive officer of MobileMedia, said in the release that the company had launched an "aggressive" plan to address issues that have affected integration with recently acquired MobileComm, such as the duplication of costs. Integration costs will be completed in the second quarter of 1997, Lorelli said.

MobileMedia reported a loss of $1.56 per share compared with a proforma consolidated loss of $1.12 per share in the same quarter last year. Last year's results were restated on a proforma basis as if the MobileComm and last year's DialPage acquisitions had taken effect by January 1, 1995.

Wells said the necessary improvements depend on the company securing liquidity from banks and other investors for continued operations. It is unclear whether the company has enough cash on hand to make the payment, he said.
"I don't think the problems are terminal, but the longer they wait the worse they get," Wells said.
